The core issue: both agents are mapping the same functional requirements into incompatible quality attribute frameworks. This represents a category error rather than a genuine conflict. The actual safety concerns (data integrity, unauthorized access, member privacy) and efficiency concerns (search response time, database query optimization) are not explicitly addressed. The truncated requirements (SAF-L2-001-05, SAF-L2-001-06, EFF-L2-002-04, EFF-L2-002-05) further obscure analysis.

steps.analysis_text: The TrustworthinessAgent focuses on security assurance, auditability, and integrity guarantees for the library management system. The six trustworthiness requirements span book search functionality, borrowing limit enforcement, book tracking, and librarian operations. The ResponsibilityAgent addresses regulatory accountability, stakeholder transparency, and ethical compliance across overlapping functional areas. A dialectic tension exists between TRU-L2-004-01 (search security assurance) and RES-L2-005-06 (search ethical compliance) - the trustworthiness framing emphasizes technical security controls while responsibility emphasizes user accessibility and fairness. Similarly, TRU-L2-004-02/03 (borrowing limits with integrity) and RES-L2-005-01/02 (borrowing limits with regulatory accountability) approach the same functional requirement from different governance perspectives. The trustworthiness perspective prioritizes data integrity and audit trails, while the responsibility perspective prioritizes fair enforcement and transparency to stakeholders. TRU-L2-004-06 and RES-L2-005-05 both address book tracking but with different emphases: trustworthiness on integrity guarantees versus responsibility on stakeholder visibility. No direct logical conflicts exist, but the requirements would benefit from explicit integration points that clarify how security controls serve accountability goals.
